column3: The Hebrew says give thanks and make music; BSB says praise and sing praises.
The Hebrew has nights in the plural; BSB has at night.
The Hebrew separately names a ten-stringed instrument and a harp; BSB combines them as a ten-stringed harp.
The Hebrew has Your deed in the singular and an uncompleted verb for jubilation; BSB has deeds and I sing.
The Hebrew explicitly includes this as the object of understanding; BSB leaves the object to the following clause.
The Hebrew presents destruction as the purpose of their sprouting; BSB frames it as a contrast with though.
The Hebrew repeats for behold and has a reflexive verb of scattering; BSB uses will be scattered.
The Hebrew describes the oil as fresh; BSB says fine oil.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular and does not explicitly name downfall or wailing as BSB does.
The Hebrew describes them as fat and fresh; BSB says healthy and green.
